sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Highness is a small specialist display designer, integrator and assembler, not a semiconductor wafer manufacturer. Customized ruggedized displays, medical/industrial applications and the 19 October glass-cutting start provide a real operating thesis. Revenue expanded to ₹16.12 crore in FY26, but reported growth is not enough to establish a compounder: almost all year-end receivables are older than six months, development and finished-goods balances complicate earnings quality, and current available funding for the next expansion phase is unknown. The ₹300.80 secondary 19 October reference implies ₹155.32 crore equity value. At that price, the modeled bull outcome requires substantial growth, margin retention and an explicit rescue yet yields only 10.61% annually, below the 15% hurdle. This is an unresolved high-risk expansion/special-situation research case, not a favorable investment classification. BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS remain NS; a mathematical bound is not a score. A documented cash/reliability bridge, collected receivables, attributable new-line returns and complete BSE execution evidence would materially change the assessment. No ordinary entry price or trade recommendation is supported.

No acquisition or operating subsidiary was identified in the reviewed company record.
Research cutoff is 20 October 2026; historical price reference is the 19 October close, ₹300.80, from a secondary BSE-history page, not an authenticated exchange trade. Certain 19 October order/press disclosures were after the close, so the cutoff information set is not a claim that an investor could already know every fact at that close. Issued shares 5163600; market cap ₹155.321088 crore.
G1 Conditional; G2/G3/G4 Hold — unresolved. Detailed gates below state the exact release evidence. Confidence is High on downloaded audited balance-sheet/P&L line items and ownership identity, Medium on interpretation of mixed-version historical cash and reported expansion, Low on current funding, incremental project economics and execution liquidity. An unmodified opinion is meaningful contrary evidence, not a reason to dismiss a material unreconciled bridge. NSE interoperability eligibility does not establish BSE suspension or an NSE listing.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The 13 canonical factors are GOV4, MOAT5, REV8, DUR6, CAP NS, CASH3, BAL NS, EXEC5, EARN4, R NS, D3, P3 and L NS. Each has multiple facts, contrary evidence, references and a confidence judgment in the factor audit. CAP is not inferred from aggregate ROIC; BAL is not inferred from historical IPO cash. R and L are not made-up neutral values.
Exact Decimal arithmetic: BQS known contribution 4.06, coverage 0.80, missing weight 0.20, raw mathematical bound[4.26, 6.06]. Growth Quality Score known contribution 5.30, coverage 0.85, missing weight 0.15, raw bound[5.45, 6.80]. Because CASH3 reflects persistent poor realization, GQS is capped at 5; the capped bound is[5, 5] but the point remains NS, not 5. IAS known contribution 0.90, coverage 0.30, missing weight 0.70, standard missing-data bound[1.60, 7.90]. Treating the unscored Q as the known BQS interval rather than an independent 1–10 variable gives dependency-aware IAS bound[2.415, 6.915]. No bound is a confidence interval or investment score. No missing weight is redistributed.
All three rankings are ineligible. There is no numeric governance cap because GOV4/G1 Conditional does not meet its trigger, nor funding cap because G3 is Hold, not Fail. The G2 hold independently prevents favorable investment classification. Exact score contributions, half-up one-decimal display bounds, and one-point sensitivity in GOV/MOAT are embedded. GOV moving to 3 would require sufficient new adverse evidence and would activate the governance override; it is not a casual score sensitivity to adopt as fact.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
The company designs, develops, integrates, manufactures/assembles and sells customized display assemblies: TFT LCDs, controller boards, touch interfaces, backlights, cables and ruggedized display systems. Value added includes optical bonding, high brightness, EMI/EMC adaptation, night-vision compatibility, thermal/physical ruggedization and application-specific engineering. Upstream panel/component dependence is substantial; this is not a domestic semiconductor fab merely because the legal name contains microelectronics. Customers are principally OEMs/system integrators in industrial automation, healthcare, rail/metro and defence-related applications. Most major names are withheld without consent; no invented customer list is used.
The operating footprint is a leased approximately 600 square-metre Rabale facility and leased office. Factory tenure disclosed through December 2029 and office through June 2027 create renewal/relocation questions; there is no freely distributable owned-operating-property surplus in valuation. The company earns from product customization and supply, then has to turn inventory and invoices into cash. FY26 geographic categories were domestic ₹8.336618 crore, exports ₹7.057858 crore and MTT ₹0.724711 crore, versus domestic ₹9.760518 crore and exports ₹4.313264 crore in FY25. MTT is retained as the source label rather than silently assigned to organic manufactured volume. Export growth and new trading mix offset domestic contraction. A generic prospectus statement that it does not export conflicts with the detailed export accounts and is treated as a drafting inconsistency, not grounds to ignore the detailed financial disclosure.
Imported inputs were 89.68% of FY25 purchases and 92.94% in nine-month FY26. Single-vendor dependency, foreign-exchange movements and lengthy customer collection can absorb margins and working capital. The distinction between cutting upstream glass and shipping qualified complete display systems matters to capacity claims.

sections.title: Moat and Industry Position
sections.text:
The strongest moat hypothesis is embedded application knowledge: qualification, ruggedization, design integration and reliability can make a cheap replacement panel insufficient for a medical or transit customer. The glass-cutting step could shorten turnaround and reduce outsourced costs. These are useful process/relationship advantages, but verified share, realized pricing premiums, customer-retention cohorts and contractual switching barriers are absent. The prospectus identifies Samtel Avionics, RR Enterprises, Winstar and Orient Display as competitors; their presence argues against treating a company claim of uniqueness as an independently established monopoly. Reviewed Samtel and Orient primary business pages support competitive application capability, not market-share numbers.
Concentration is material: largest customer 29.56% of FY25 sales and 44.78% in nine-month FY26, top 10 customers 84.51% and 82.43%; topvendor 89.60% and 72.71%. No long-term customer/supplier agreements are the disclosed norm. Breadth across end-use labels does not equal diversified revenue. A dominant vendor or customer can capture the benefit of engineering work, while input FX can offset nominal price increases.
Listed electronics peers are context, not a valuation template. Centum FY26 continuing consolidated revenue ₹952.749 crore and continuing PAT ₹100.711 crore differ from total consolidated loss ₹51.806 crore because discontinued operations lost ₹152.517 crore. That ordinary scope distinction is not an accounting error. Cyient DLM FY26 revenue ₹1261.5 crore, normalized EBITDA ₹130.2 crore/10.3%, and separately reported EBITDA ₹126.8 crore come from a much larger, different manufacturing mix; earnings include separately described earn-out/labour normalization. Neither provides a directly comparable small custom-display multiple. Current peer prices/PE s were not authenticated and remain ND. MOAT5 recognizes contestable capability, not a durable structural excess-return moat.

sections.title: Revenue Growth and Scale
sections.text:
Annual revenue, crore, FY21–FY26:3.5219312, 7.2120481, 9.674249, 10.704622, 14.073782, 16.119187. Absolute additions are therefore ₹3.6901169, ₹2.4622009, ₹1.030373, ₹3.369160 and ₹2.045405 crore. Five-year CAGR 35.55% is impressive but starts in the pandemic-depressed FY21; FY20 revenue ₹5.8797639 crore gives six-year CAGR 18.30%, and FY23–26 three-year CAGR 18.55%. FY26 growth 14.53% is slower than FY25. Ten-year comparable revenue is ND, not zero. The period is chosen before scoring; starting REV9 for≥30% CAGR receives one net downward adjustment to 8 for the evidenced base/trajectory distortion, not an additional generic small-company penalty.
No acquisition-led expansion was identified. Volume, price, customization mix and FX are not consistently separated, so reported revenue is the demonstrated measure and organic constant-price growth is not asserted as verified. FY26 domestic revenue fell about 14.59%, exports rose about 63.63%, and MTT added ₹0.724711 crore. One should not call this broad domestic demand acceleration. June's 261-unit order averaging gross ₹72414 per unit illustrates how realization can differ from a low-cost standard panel; it does not establish an across-company ASP.
The capacity certificate dated 21 February 2026 reports installed/available industrial capacity 45000/33750 units, but output fell 16366 in FY23 to 12567 in FY24 and 10304 in FY25; nine-month FY26 reports only 25 industrial units while LCD open-cell output rose to 4168. Medical output was 269, 213, 214 and 155. Product category shifts can explain some movement, but a revenue-to-units bridge is needed before interpreting utilization as scalable recurring volume. The certificate is evidence of stated capacity, not of incremental returns or demand. Customer concentration and order announcements do not justify multiplying the historical CAGR indefinitely.

sections.title: Growth Quality and Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
The runway has three layers: grow qualified display solutions at Rabale, internalize upstream steps such as glass cutting, and eventually establish Goa COG/FOG, testing/R&D and metal-fabrication capabilities. The first has actual sales; the second has a 19 October commercial-start filing; the third remains a capital and execution proposal. The prospectus describes a 5000 square-metre Goa plot 18 A allotment dated 6 February 2026, with an initial premium/rent installment and formal lease pending at that stage. No reviewed underlying document establishes a fully funded project, total committed cost or irrevocable ECMS award. An application and potential 25% eligible-capex incentive are not approved cash; modeled subsidy is zero.
FY26 normalized NOPAT divided by average operating invested capital gives 30.45% ROIC, and the one-year change ratio gives 26.91%. However, R&D capitalization/amortization, changes in inventory and restated cash classification prevent attribution to a comparable capital cohort. Three- and five-year incremental returns are NS; CAP is NS despite encouraging headline returns. Capitalized development ₹1.471326 crore and its amortization ₹0.708894 crore are real reinvestment issues, not free intangible upside.
The bottom-up model explicitly assumes 70% display revenue and ₹30000 per finished unit, then computes required units against 33750 available industrial units. These are analyst sensitivities, not verified product-mix forecasts.300 glass cuts/day is upstream throughput and is never substituted for 300 finished systems/day. Annual capex envelopes include maintenance, development, existing IPO project and future expansion; the disclosed ₹5.267518 crore Rabale IPO project is not added again. Goa costs remain unknown, so ₹2/4 crore additional annual-capex stresses are labeled assumptions. The result is Growth Quality NS, raw bound 5.45–6.80 and cap 5 due persistent CASH3, not an attractive unqualified growth score.

sections.title: Management, Governance and Execution
sections.text:
Promoters retain 3354090 shares/64.96% and public holders 1809510/35.04% at 30 September 2026; 3510 public shares are locked. No disclosed pledge, warrants or convertible dilution is included. Alignment from a large stake is useful but not sufficient. FY26 director remuneration ₹0.84 crore equals 20.47% of PAT, and gross director advances ₹0.600880 crore equal 14.64% of PAT, while company borrowing includes expensive unsecured facilities. Disclosed approvals and auditor statements of arm's-length/ordinary-course and section 185/186 compliance are retained as contrary evidence. Gross director advances and the net related-party remuneration account need not match mechanically; no unsupported diversion allegation is made.
Historical PF/ESI registration gaps, delayed export proceeds and TDS/GST deficiencies show a need for stronger controls. Legacy unpaid PF/ESI amount is unquantified. TDS deficiencies ₹0.127069 crore and export-linked GST ₹0.2642492 crore plus ₹0.0995651 crore interest are disclosed; amounts already in liabilities are not charged a second time. A GST appeal ₹0.292289 crore and customs goods liability ₹0.5018931 crore are separate contingent/stress questions, subject to overlap verification. The audit-trail note contains a stale December 2025 applicability statement alongside FY26 operation language; this is a clarification issue, not proof of fraudulent software use.
Auditor changes have specific explanations: Satya Gandhi lacked the required peer-review status; VN Purohit's later exit referenced mutual coordination/geography; Jain Vinay took over. The actual Sanjiv Swarup resignation letter cites personal/professional constraints and statutory directorship limits, expressly stating no other material reason. Those explanations are not replaced with a speculative governance narrative.
Promises versus delivery: June ₹1.89 crore/261 unit order targeted June–July; no reviewed execution/collection reconciliation. August ₹1.07 crore TVM order and September ₹6 crore medical order are real disclosures, not completed revenue. October ₹0.54 crore TVM and ₹0.21 crore medical orders are similarly subject to delivery; several values include tax/freight. Glass-line start on 19 October is delivered as a commissioning milestone, while promised savings and Goa scale are not demonstrated. May's Axiom memorandum is exploratory, not a purchase contract. EXEC5 recognizes the difference.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The embedded historical table contains FY21–26 revenue, EBITDA/EBIT, PAT, normalized PAT, finance cost, depreciation, CFO, capex, FCF, cash, debt, equity, working-capital balances, share counts and separate per-share measures. FY21/22 are original statutory, FY23/24 IPO-restated and FY25/26 latest statutory. This mixed-version choice is explicit, not a fabricated clean restated series. Gross profit, contract assets and finance-lease debt are ND where the evidence does not support a consistent line. Early deferred-development amortization makes EBITDA comparisons imperfect. Every year has opening cash+CFO+CFI+CFF=closing cash with residual retained.
FY26 operating EBITDA ₹6.617641 crore and EBIT ₹5.576289 crore differ from EBITDA including other income. PBT ₹5.345734 crore includes ₹0.798310 crore other income, principally ₹0.720431 crore FX, with ₹0.716176 crore unrealized. Normalizing all other income out and applying 25% tax gives ₹3.410568 crore PAT proxy, not an audited adjusted number. Reported PAT ₹4.103919 crore, up from ₹2.458208 crore, must be interpreted with rising finished goods ₹7.704975 crore, capitalized development and later cash realization. FY26 D&A ₹1.041352 crore includes substantial development amortization.
CFO ₹4.702861 crore less ₹2.110266 crore cash capex gives ₹2.592595 crore FCF before financing interest; after ₹1.028865 crore interest, ₹1.563730 crore. Three-year mixed-version CFO/PAT is 0.7233 and after-interest conversion 0.5404; FCF before financing interest is negative ₹0.416014 crore. Five-year arithmetic is embedded but not claimed as clean cycle evidence because classifications differ. Current cash taxes ₹0.107257 crore versus provision ₹1.361190 crore and legacy income-tax payable ₹2.067033 crore mean reported CFO is not all distributable.
Receivables ₹10.365629 crore comprise only ₹0.008310 crore under six months, ₹6.939609 crore six–twelve months and ₹3.417710 crore one–two years. The balance-sheet increase ₹6.164998 crore less unrealized FX ₹0.716176 crore equals cash-flow receivable absorption ₹5.448822 crore: this bridge is resolved. Aerohaste FY25 sales ₹4.1597248 crore had collections ₹1.1488685 crore by March 2026, leaving ₹3.0332561 crore. Management cites technical collection hurdles, discussions and positive assessment and carries full value. That claim is retained; absence of later verified cash means a loss stress is appropriate, not a factual writeoff.
ONWC excludes tax, director advances and unidentified other payables, but includes operating prepaids once; it rises ₹8.453369 to ₹12.754396 crore. Adding tangible/intangible assets and operating deposits gives IC ₹10.971333/₹16.501407 crore. Financing-view IC reconciles within ₹20/₹10 rounding. Average-capital normalized ROIC 30.45%, ROCE 40.60% and interest coverage 5.42× are diagnostics, not CAP proof.
Several apparent mismatches are resolved: RFS12 explains FY25 statutory PAT 2.458208 to 2.522600 via tax/deferred-tax; FY24 PAT 1.771880 to 2.387962 via amortization, MSME interest, tax/deferred tax and gratuity. FY23 CFO/CFI changes offset ₹3.380867 crore; FY25 ₹1.756626 croreborrowing reclassification shifts CFO to financing. In contrast, FY25's FY24 comparative uses opening cash ₹1.006947 crore versus original FY23/restated ₹0.03807 crore. Original FY24 cash flow at rounded ₹000 shows CFO ₹0.8421/CFI−₹0.4542/CFF−₹0.1643 crore; the later comparative and IPO restated versions differ. A combined opening cash/CFO/investing bridge remains missing. FY26's FY25 EPS 4.76 uses post-IPO shares rather than actual FY25 weighted shares 3510000; fresh issuance is not a bonus adjustment. These specific unresolved material presentations support G2 Hold despite an unmodified audit.
IPO fresh ₹19.8432 crore less company cost ₹2.776561 crore equals ₹17.066639 crore company net cash. OFS ₹1.8288 crore is seller money, not company funding; seller-net ₹1.572905 crore plus company net equals whole-offer ₹18.639544 crore. March cash already includes proceeds. Other payables ₹1.634918 crore could include settlement but are not identified; all settle once in the model. Debt ₹7.943440 crore includes current maturities, CC ₹2.990821 crore and director loan ₹0.023133 crore. Do not add current maturities again or treat historical cash as October unrestricted cash.

sections.title: Valuation and Market Expectations
sections.text:
The secondary reference ₹300.80 implies market cap ₹155.321088 crore, 37.847× reported PAT, 45.541× normalized PAT proxy and 5.718× March book. Substituting historical March cash/debt gives EV ₹141.458144 crore and 21.376× operating EBITDA; this is a labeled historical-balance diagnostic, not authenticated October EV or cash available to shareholders. No operational property, IPO proceeds, prepaids, director advances or warrants are added as surplus value.
The primary return method is a funded five-year terminal enterprise-value bridge, supported by cash-floor-aware DCF rather than a headline PE-only forecast. Opening March 26 cash is carried through 202/365 of FY27 to 19 October; only the remaining 163/365 of FY27 belongs after entry. FY28–31 are full fiscal years, then 202/366 of FY32 to 19 October 2031. Terminal revenue is a prorated trailing-year run rate, not all of FY32. No dividends or automatic borrowing are assumed. Existing term debt amortizes 3.052481/1.2/0.677005 crore in FY27–29; continuing CC is conditional. Legacy tax, statutory, other payable and director loan amounts settle once before entry, not again at exit.
Annual analyst assumptions FY27–32: bear growth−10/5/7/8/8/8%, EBITDA margin 12/14/15/15/15/15%, ONWC 110/115/115/110/105/100% of sales, capex 8/6/4/3/3/3 crore, exit 7×; base growth 25/25/22/20/18/15%, margin 28/28/27/27/26/26%, ONWC 85/85/82/78/75/72%, capex 8/6/6/4/4/4 crore, exit 10×; bull growth 40/35/30/25/22/20%, margin 35/35/34/33/32/30%, ONWC 80/78/75/72/70/68%, capex 9/8/8/7/6/6 crore, exit 14×. These include maintenance/development and expansion, not disclosed committed Goa budgets. D&A, interest, taxes, receivable-loss and contingent stresses are explicit in every annual row.
Required cash is max(₹0.5 crore, 3% of trailing revenue), retained at terminal. The terminal equity bridge uses signed cash less this floor, including a negative deficit on unfunded paths; it never drops an unpaid funding gap. Exact-day discounting is scaled to the five-year October anniversary. All ordinary returns/entry prices are null because current funding is unverified. Every base scenario first breaches the cash floor in FY28; peak non-rescue gaps are ₹12.0361/₹5.4934/₹7.3860 crore bear/base/bull. Therefore even non-rescue conditional returns/entry prices are null. Positive terminal valuation diagnostics from an unfunded path are not return recommendations.
A completely separate rescue illustration issues rounded whole shares at 50% below ₹300.80 with 3% fees whenever the floor would be breached. Gross equity required ₹12.4083/₹5.6633/₹7.6145 crore adds 825023/376548/506281 shares. Resulting five-year rescue IRRs are−37.18%/−6.14%/+10.61%; rescue-only 15% hurdle entry diagnostics ₹14.63/₹108.91/₹247.65. These assume willing subscribers and hold issue pricing fixed at the reference-price discount, rather than repricing rescue equity at each alternative entry. They are not available financing or ordinary buy prices. Dilution is essential, not suppressed.
DCF uses 14/16/18% WACC, 3/4/5% terminal growth and 12/16/20% terminal ROIC, including terminal growth reinvestment and cash-floor growth. The central 16/4/16 case gives financing-agnostic ₹32.99/share, but terminal PV is 164.6% of operating EV because forecast FCFF is negative; it is particularly fragile and not an actionable entry. The equity bridge uses signed entry cash minus floor, debt once, and retained gratuity once; excess cash is not double counted.
Sensitivity covers growth 10–50% against exit 7/10/14/18×, execution costs 0/1/3/5% each side, hurdles 12/15/18%, extra annual Goa capex ₹2/4 crore, ONWC+20 points, margin−8 points, collection loss, CC nonrenewal, 25% cash unavailable and combined stress. No funded ordinary grid point supports the 15% hurdle. With explicit rescue, fixed 10× exit requires about 59.1% constant growth and ₹62.21 crore gross equity; 14× needs 42% growth and ₹25.14 crore; 18× needs 33.1% and ₹14.02 crore. These reverse expectations reveal the capital burden rather than claim a target. Rescue discounts 25/50/70% and fees 0/3/6% are separately modeled.

sections.title: Bear Case and Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest counterargument to a Hold is that old receivables are ultimately collected, the commissioned glass line immediately lowers input cost, medical/metro orders repeat and growth absorbs fixed engineering cost. In that outcome the high reported margin need not collapse and the March equity raise provides a useful buffer. This possibility is why the analysis does not assert fraud, current insolvency or a worthless business.
The permanent-loss path is nevertheless coherent: a dominant export customer delays or disputes payment; finished goods fail to convert at carrying value; import cost/FX or customer pricing compress margins; Goa capex and working capital consume the IPO cash; the demand line cannot roll; then discounted equity finances a project with insufficient incremental cash return. A holder can suffer both business-value loss and dilution, then find that one-sided SME prices do not permit a low-impact exit. Secondary price appreciation does not invalidate this path.
The linked model separately stresses Aerohaste ₹3.0332561 crore loss, all receivables older than a year ₹3.417710 crore loss, CC call, extra annual capex, margin and working capital. Collection loss is a cash drag once, not an extra terminal writeoff after reducing cash. GST/customs stress is explicitly additional only if not already included; booked tax/statutory liabilities are never silently charged twice. A combined stress is not a probability forecast, but establishes financing/dilution sensitivity. Actual current funding remains unknown, so G3 Hold rather than Fail.
The thesis-break variable is not one weak quarter; it is evidence that incremental invoicing/development expenditure cannot produce cash returns above the 14–18% cost-of-capital range, or that essential cash uses cannot be funded without value-destructive rescue. Prompt audited collection and capital project data could falsify the bear case. Unresolved data cannot be assigned a favorable probability.

sections.title: 5× and 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
Fivefold and tenfold price gains over five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annual shareholder returns, respectively. At unchanged 5163600 shares, an assumed 20× terminal PE and 20% net margin, 5× requires PAT ₹38.830272 crore and revenue ₹194.15136 crore; 10× requires PAT ₹77.660544 crore and revenue ₹388.30272 crore. From FY26 sales ₹16.119187 crore those are 64.50% and 88.96% revenue CAGRs. These algebraic requirements do not establish economic feasibility; dilution raises the profit/sales need further.
At the illustrative 70% display mix/₹30000 ASP, that sales scale would require about 45302 or 90604 finished units, versus disclosed available industrial capacity 33750 and FY25 industrial output 10304. The separate 300 glass cuts/day claim is not a finished-product capacity substitute. Customer qualification, order conversion, material availability, working capital, funded Goa capacity and project returns would all have to improve substantially. No verified TAM-share bridge or signed pipeline substantiates that outcome today.
Multiple expansion alone can produce a nominal 5× scenario on paper, but it is not a durable multibagger thesis. The base reverse expectations already require large rescue equity under fast growth. Thus 5× is speculative and 10× still more demanding; neither earns a high GQS, CAP or investment classification. Falsification requires actual repeat orders and collected cash at meaningful scale, not merely memoranda or product-category launches.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Receivable collection: baseline ₹10.365629 crore with ₹10.357319 croreolder than six months and Aerohaste ₹3.0332561 crore. Require dated cash receipt/ageing bridge; further ageing without collection or unexplained credit notes is a warning. A material confirmed impairment without offsetting funding changes the survival assessment.
2. Financial reliability: obtain auditor-supported FY24 original/comparative/restated cash rollforward and FY25/26 weighted average EPS. G2 cannot clear merely because the next opinion is unmodified.
3. Current funding: reconcile March ₹21.806384 crore cash through actual IPO spend, settlement, tax, debt, restricted balances and October availability; document CC sanctions/covenants. A cash-floor breach without committed funding triggers escalation, not automatic assumed debt.
4. Working capital: baseline ONWC ₹12.754396 crore/79.13% of FY26 sales. Demand growth in collections and inventory turns, not just payables finance; a persistent+20 point ONWC stress is modeled.
5. Development economics: track capitalized cost ₹1.471326 crore, amortization ₹0.708894 crore, project start, sales/gross contribution/cash and required maintenance. Need three/five-year cohorts to score CAP.
6. Glass line: establish paid project cost, uptime, yield, glass cuts versus qualified shipped units and realized net savings. Management's 10% initial/30–40% potential cost saving claims require baseline and scope.
7. Goa/ECMS: read final lease, approved layout/equipment quotations, formal approvals, project schedule and committed funding. Application or landing page is not approval; subsidy only counts after documented eligibility/approval/collection timing.
8. Orders: reconcile opening backlog+new orders−shipments−cancellations=closing backlog, excluding tax/freight and duplicate follow-ons; verify June/July 261 units and September 16–20 week order delivery/collections.
9. Stewardship: director advance repayment, statutory settlement, related party terms, remuneration and use-of-proceeds monitoring. Preserve explanations unless new contrary evidence arises.
10. Tradability: official BSE 20/60 session turnover, lot and restriction status, one-sided circuits and book depth. Recheck before any position; one/two-lot ₹360960/₹721920 concentrations matter more than a theoretical ₹5 lakh average exit calculation.

sections.title: Final Classification and Conditional Action
sections.text:
Final classification: Hold — unresolved financial reliability, funding and tradability; high-risk expansion/special-situation thesis, not a demonstrated compounder. Business Quality Score NS, Growth Quality Score NS and Investment Attractiveness Score NS. Quality, growth-quality and investment ranking eligibility are all false. These labels do not mean the business lacks revenue or useful technology; they mean the required evidence does not support the favorable inference.
No ordinary entry range is issued. A lower market price alone cannot repair G2, current funding or tradability. Rescue-only price diagnostics remain contingent on hypothetical equity availability, fees, dilution and the full assumption path; they are not substitute recommendations. GQS's cap 5 does not become a point 5. The datedraw bounds 4.26–6.06 BQS, 5.45–6.80 GQS before cap, and 1.60–7.90 IAS are carried exactly into the final summary.
A favorable reclassification requires all of: resolved material cash/EPS bridges; verified post-IPO available cash and funded capex/debt stress; meaningful subsequent receivable collection; credible attributable incremental returns; and complete official BSE execution evidence. After those arrive, rerun cash flow, dilution and valuation at then-current price rather than retain this historical reference. Any investment decision must independently consider suitability, diversification and ability to bear a permanent loss. This is research, not personalized financial advice or an instruction to trade.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions and Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary sources are the downloaded final IPO prospectus, original FY20–26 annual reports, underlying ownership HTML and individual production/order/resignation filings, not just investor landing pages. Each source entry has URL, hash, date/period, locator and access status. OCR/transcription of older annuals was checked against selected rendered pages; those images and raw issuer documents are excluded from the source-free analytical package. The record retains safe financial extracts, source URL s/hashes, source-specific claims and reproducible model code. Fresh retrieval and hash comparison are needed to authenticate originals; source-free reproduction checks arithmetic, not authenticity.
BSE official archive and earnings-call transcript retrieval returned 403; the denied route was not bypassed. The transcript was not read and cannot be quoted as corroboration. The 19 October quote/OHLCV series is secondary; the NSE 60-date archive provides only a calendar sampling proxy for BSE, not BSE trades. Missing dates are unknown, not zero volume. Official traded value mean/median remain null; observed low× volume/high× volume are bounded proxies, never actual turnover. Interoperability lot/share data agree with company capital disclosures, but its price band/NSE eligibility fields are not used as BSE live authorization.
Financial definitions: operating EBIT=PBT+finance cost−other income; EBITDA=EBIT+D&A; normalized PAT proxy=(PBT−other income)×75%; FCF=CFO−cash capex, before financing interest unless stated. ROIC uses normalized NOPAT/average operating IC; cash/debt and nonoperating claims are separately reconciled. No acquisition capital, property surplus, lease financial liability or new warrant is fabricated. Old cash-flow classifications are tagged; historical ratio arithmetic does not cure comparability.
Decisive open questions are October available funds/uses, Goa committed cost and ECMS approval, material aged collection, development cohort returns, inventory realization, FY24 cash comparative and EPS denominators, order delivery/backlog, and official BSE execution history. Budgets, margins, ASP, unit mix, interest, tax and rescue pricing are explicit assumptions, not management guidance. A source claim contested by financial detail is preserved with status; resolved scope/reclassification differences are not reused as allegations. All historical information is bounded by 20 October 2026; later retrieval does not authorize post-cutoff facts.

summary: Highness is a small specialist display designer, integrator and assembler, not a semiconductor wafer manufacturer. Customized ruggedized displays, medical/industrial applications and the 19 October glass-cutting start provide a real operating thesis. Revenue expanded to ₹16.12 crore in FY26, but reported growth is not enough to establish a compounder: almost all year-end receivables are older than six months, development and finished-goods balances complicate earnings quality, and current available funding for the next expansion phase is unknown. The ₹300.80 secondary 19 October reference implies ₹155.32 crore equity value. At that price, the modeled bull outcome requires substantial growth, margin retention and an explicit rescue yet yields only 10.61% annually, below the 15% hurdle. This is an unresolved high-risk expansion/special-situation research case, not a favorable investment classification. BQS, Growth Quality Score and IAS remain NS; a mathematical bound is not a score. A documented cash/reliability bridge, collected receivables, attributable new-line returns and complete BSE execution evidence would materially change the assessment. No ordinary entry price or trade recommendation is supported.
